paragraphs.title: Israel Reaches the Wilderness and Complains

easy.question: Where did the Israelites arrive after traveling from Elim?
answers: Mount Sinai
The wilderness of Sin
The land of Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that they came to the wilderness of Sin.

easy.question: Against whom did the Israelites complain in the wilderness?
answers: Pharaoh
Joshua and Caleb
Moses and Aaron
easy.explanation: The verse says that the whole congregation complained against Moses and Aaron.

easy.question: What did the Israelites claim they had in Egypt?
answers: Flesh and bread to eat their fill
Houses and fields
Water and fruit
easy.explanation: They remembered sitting by the flesh pots and eating bread to the full in Egypt.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites complain against Moses and Aaron?
answers: They feared dying of hunger in the wilderness
They wanted to return to Elim
They did not want to reach Mount Sinai
medium.explanation: They accused Moses and Aaron of bringing them into the wilderness to kill the whole assembly with hunger.

medium.question: In the phrase “the whole congregation ... murmured,” what does “murmured” mean?
answers: Traveled quickly
Complained
Rested quietly
medium.explanation: “Murmured” means complained or grumbled; the verse says they complained against Moses and Aaron.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: They complained, left Elim, and then reached the wilderness of Sin
They reached Sinai, returned to Egypt, and then complained
They left Elim, reached the wilderness of Sin, and then complained
medium.explanation: They first traveled from Elim to the wilderness of Sin, and afterward complained against Moses and Aaron.

challenge.question: What does the statement “Would to God we had died ... in the land of Egypt” reveal about the Israelites’ feelings?
answers: They preferred dying in Egypt after eating their fill to dying of hunger in the wilderness
They wanted to fight the Egyptians
They believed there was no danger in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: They compared their food in Egypt with their fear of dying from hunger in the wilderness.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the wilderness of Sin being described as “between Elim and Sinai”?
answers: They had already reached Canaan
They were still traveling, before reaching Sinai
They had returned to Egypt
challenge.explanation: The description shows that they were on the way, not yet at Mount Sinai or in Canaan.

challenge.question: To whom is the accusation “ye have brought us forth” addressed?
answers: Pharaoh and his officials
All the Israelites
Moses and Aaron together
challenge.explanation: The plural “ye” refers to Moses and Aaron, whom the Israelites blamed together.

questions.question: What does the statement “Would to God we had died ... in the land of Egypt” reveal about the Israelites’ feelings?
answers: They preferred dying in Egypt after eating their fill to dying of hunger in the wilderness
They wanted to fight the Egyptians
They believed there was no danger in the wilderness
questions.explanation: They compared their food in Egypt with their fear of dying from hunger in the wilderness.

questions.question: What can we infer from the wilderness of Sin being described as “between Elim and Sinai”?
answers: They had already reached Canaan
They were still traveling, before reaching Sinai
They had returned to Egypt
questions.explanation: The description shows that they were on the way, not yet at Mount Sinai or in Canaan.

questions.question: To whom is the accusation “ye have brought us forth” addressed?
answers: Pharaoh and his officials
All the Israelites
Moses and Aaron together
questions.explanation: The plural “ye” refers to Moses and Aaron, whom the Israelites blamed together.

paragraphs.title: The Promise of Bread from Heaven

easy.question: What did the Lord promise to rain down from heaven for the people?
answers: Bread
Water
Flesh
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “I will rain bread from heaven for you.”

easy.question: On which day would the Israelites gather twice as much?
answers: The first day
The sixth day
The Sabbath
easy.explanation: The verse says that on the sixth day they would gather twice as much.

easy.question: What would the Israelites know in the evening?
answers: That they would see the glory of the Lord
That they had to return to Egypt
That the Lord had brought them out of Egypt
easy.explanation: Moses and Aaron said, “At even ... ye shall know that the Lord hath brought you out.”

medium.question: Why did the Lord command the people to gather a certain amount every day?
answers: So they would learn to build houses
To test whether they would follow His law
So they would not eat bread
medium.explanation: The verse says that the daily gathering would test whether they would walk in the Lord’s law.

medium.question: In the phrase “it shall be twice as much,” what does “twice” mean?
answers: A double amount
A small amount
New bread
medium.explanation: “Twice” means double; on the sixth day they would gather twice the usual amount.

medium.question: According to Moses, what would be the order of the food provided?
answers: Flesh in the evening and bread in the morning
Bread in the evening and flesh in the morning
Water in the evening and bread in the morning
medium.explanation: Moses said that the Lord would give flesh in the evening and bread in the morning.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the words “what are we?”
answers: Moses and Aaron wanted to be stronger leaders
Moses and Aaron admitted that they were not the source of the food or miracle
Moses and Aaron did not know where the people were
challenge.explanation: The words show that Moses and Aaron had no independent power to provide food; the complaint was really against the Lord.

challenge.question: Why is it emphasized that the people would see the glory of the Lord in the morning after their complaints were heard?
answers: To show that the Lord responds to their complaints and provides for them
To announce that the people would remain hungry
To replace Moses with another leader
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the people’s complaints with the appearance of the Lord’s glory and the provision of food.

challenge.question: What distinguishes gathering food on an ordinary day from gathering it on the sixth day?
answers: On an ordinary day the people could not eat the food
On the sixth day they did not need to prepare it
On the sixth day they gathered twice as much and prepared it beforehand
challenge.explanation: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much and prepared it, unlike on an ordinary day.

questions.question: What can we understand from the words “what are we?”
answers: Moses and Aaron wanted to be stronger leaders
Moses and Aaron admitted that they were not the source of the food or miracle
Moses and Aaron did not know where the people were
questions.explanation: The words show that Moses and Aaron had no independent power to provide food; the complaint was really against the Lord.

questions.question: Why is it emphasized that the people would see the glory of the Lord in the morning after their complaints were heard?
answers: To show that the Lord responds to their complaints and provides for them
To announce that the people would remain hungry
To replace Moses with another leader
questions.explanation: The verses connect the people’s complaints with the appearance of the Lord’s glory and the provision of food.

questions.question: What distinguishes gathering food on an ordinary day from gathering it on the sixth day?
answers: On an ordinary day the people could not eat the food
On the sixth day they did not need to prepare it
On the sixth day they gathered twice as much and prepared it beforehand
questions.explanation: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much and prepared it, unlike on an ordinary day.

paragraphs.title: The Glory of the Lord Appears in the Cloud

easy.question: Who told Aaron to speak to the whole congregation of Israel?
answers: Moses
The Lord
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that Moses told Aaron to speak to the people.

easy.question: What appeared in the cloud when the Israelites looked toward the wilderness?
answers: Rain
The glory of the Lord
Smoke
easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “the glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud.”

easy.question: When would the Israelites eat flesh?
answers: In the morning
At midnight
In the evening
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “At even ye shall eat flesh.”

medium.question: What happened after Aaron spoke to the whole congregation of Israel?
answers: They looked toward the wilderness and saw the glory of the Lord in the cloud
They returned to Egypt
They immediately ate bread
medium.explanation: After Aaron spoke, the people looked toward the wilderness and saw the Lord’s glory in the cloud.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites told to come near before the Lord?
answers: Because they wanted to build an altar
Because the Lord had heard their complaints
Because it was time to leave Egypt
medium.explanation: Moses told them to come near because the Lord had heard their complaints.

medium.question: In the phrase “he hath heard your murmurings,” what are “murmurings”?
answers: Songs
Blessings
Words of protest and complaint
medium.explanation: “Murmurings” means words of protest or complaint; the Lord heard the people’s complaints about their situation.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the promise “ye shall know that I am the Lord your God” after the promise of flesh and bread?
answers: The provision would also show that the Lord was their God
The Israelites would have to prepare the food themselves
They would receive no food in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The verse connects receiving food with recognizing that the Lord is their God.

challenge.question: What order of speakers appears in these verses?
answers: Aaron, Moses, the Lord
Moses, Aaron, the Lord
The Lord, Aaron, Moses
challenge.explanation: First Moses speaks to Aaron, then Aaron speaks to the people, and finally the Lord speaks to Moses.

challenge.question: What is the exact difference between the promised times for the two foods in verse 12?
answers: Flesh in the morning and bread in the evening
Both flesh and bread in the morning
Flesh in the evening and bread in the morning
challenge.explanation: The verse gives two different times: flesh in the evening and bread in the morning.

questions.question: What can we understand from the promise “ye shall know that I am the Lord your God” after the promise of flesh and bread?
answers: The provision would also show that the Lord was their God
The Israelites would have to prepare the food themselves
They would receive no food in the wilderness
questions.explanation: The verse connects receiving food with recognizing that the Lord is their God.

questions.question: What order of speakers appears in these verses?
answers: Aaron, Moses, the Lord
Moses, Aaron, the Lord
The Lord, Aaron, Moses
questions.explanation: First Moses speaks to Aaron, then Aaron speaks to the people, and finally the Lord speaks to Moses.

questions.question: What is the exact difference between the promised times for the two foods in verse 12?
answers: Flesh in the morning and bread in the evening
Both flesh and bread in the morning
Flesh in the evening and bread in the morning
questions.explanation: The verse gives two different times: flesh in the evening and bread in the morning.

paragraphs.title: Quail and Manna in the Wilderness

easy.question: What came up in the evening and covered the camp?
answers: Quail
Dew
Manna
easy.explanation: The verse says that the quail came up and covered the camp.

easy.question: What was around the camp in the morning?
answers: Rain
A layer of dew
A cloud
easy.explanation: In the morning, the dew lay around the camp.

easy.question: How did Moses explain what the Israelites found?
answers: It was snow
It was sand
It was the bread the Lord had given them to eat
easy.explanation: Moses said, “This is the bread which the Lord hath given you to eat.”

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: In the evening quail came up; in the morning the dew lifted and a small thing appeared on the ground
In the morning quail came up, and in the evening the dew fell
First they ate, and afterward the quail came
medium.explanation: The verses first describe the quail in the evening and then the dew and the small thing found in the morning.

medium.question: In the phrase “a small round thing,” what does “small” describe?
answers: Completely smooth
Small in size and delicate in texture
Very wet
medium.explanation: The verse describes something small and delicate, like hoarfrost on the ground.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites ask, “What is it?”
answers: Because they knew it was bread
Because they thought it was quail
Because they did not know what the thing was
medium.explanation: The verse explains that they asked because they did not know what it was.

challenge.question: What can we learn from the difference between the quail in the evening and the small thing in the morning?
answers: The Lord provided food at different times and in different forms
Only the quail was meant to be eaten
The thing in the morning was a sign of rain
challenge.explanation: Quail appeared in the evening, while the bread appeared in the morning after the dew.

challenge.question: What does the question “What is it?” show about the Israelites’ reaction?
answers: They immediately gave the food an exact name
They were surprised and did not recognize what they found
They refused to accept the food
challenge.explanation: The question expresses surprise and uncertainty, as the verse explains.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “one to another” mean in this context?
answers: Each person ate alone
Moses spoke only with his brother
The Israelites asked one another in shared wonder
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes the Israelites turning to one another and asking what they had seen.

questions.question: What can we learn from the difference between the quail in the evening and the small thing in the morning?
answers: The Lord provided food at different times and in different forms
Only the quail was meant to be eaten
The thing in the morning was a sign of rain
questions.explanation: Quail appeared in the evening, while the bread appeared in the morning after the dew.

questions.question: What does the question “What is it?” show about the Israelites’ reaction?
answers: They immediately gave the food an exact name
They were surprised and did not recognize what they found
They refused to accept the food
questions.explanation: The question expresses surprise and uncertainty, as the verse explains.

questions.question: What does the phrase “one to another” mean in this context?
answers: Each person ate alone
Moses spoke only with his brother
The Israelites asked one another in shared wonder
questions.explanation: The phrase describes the Israelites turning to one another and asking what they had seen.

easy.question: Who commanded the Israelites how to gather the manna?
answers: The Lord
Moses alone
The elders of the people
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “This is the thing which the Lord hath commanded.”

easy.question: How much manna was assigned to each person?
answers: Two omers
An omer for each person
Half an omer
easy.explanation: The instruction was one omer for each person.

easy.question: What did the Israelites do after receiving the instruction?
answers: They measured it immediately
They left it in the camp
They gathered manna
easy.explanation: The verse says that they gathered it, some more and some less.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites told to gather according to the number of people in each tent?
answers: So that each person would have enough food
So that manna would remain for the next day
So that only heads of families would gather
medium.explanation: The amount was based on the number of people and their food needs.

medium.question: What was the order of events in these verses?
answers: They measured, were commanded, and then gathered
They were commanded to gather, gathered, and then measured
They gathered, ate, and then received the command
medium.explanation: First the instruction was given, then the Israelites gathered, and finally they measured it.

medium.question: In the phrase “he that gathered much had nothing over,” what does “had nothing over” mean?
answers: He hid it
He ate it
He had no excess remaining
medium.explanation: The one who gathered more did not end up with more than he needed.

challenge.question: How could some gather more and others less, yet “he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack”?
answers: The amount finally measured matched each person’s needs
The one who gathered more gave all his manna to the one who gathered less
Only a small amount of manna was actually measured
challenge.explanation: Although people gathered different amounts, each person ultimately had exactly what he needed.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the phrase “every man ... for them which are in his tents”?
answers: Everyone had to gather alone
The number of people in each tent had to be taken into account
Only people outside the tents received manna
challenge.explanation: The phrase connects the amount gathered with the number of people in each tent or family.

challenge.question: What central principle stands out in the distribution of manna?
answers: Everyone had to gather exactly the same amount
The one who gathered more always received more
The amount was determined by need, not by the amount first gathered
challenge.explanation: The verses emphasize that each person received according to his eating and need.

questions.question: How could some gather more and others less, yet “he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack”?
answers: The amount finally measured matched each person’s needs
The one who gathered more gave all his manna to the one who gathered less
Only a small amount of manna was actually measured
questions.explanation: Although people gathered different amounts, each person ultimately had exactly what he needed.

questions.question: What can we understand from the phrase “every man ... for them which are in his tents”?
answers: Everyone had to gather alone
The number of people in each tent had to be taken into account
Only people outside the tents received manna
questions.explanation: The phrase connects the amount gathered with the number of people in each tent or family.

questions.question: What central principle stands out in the distribution of manna?
answers: Everyone had to gather exactly the same amount
The one who gathered more always received more
The amount was determined by need, not by the amount first gathered
questions.explanation: The verses emphasize that each person received according to his eating and need.

easy.question: Until when did Moses command the people not to leave any manna?
answers: Until morning
Until noon
Until evening
easy.explanation: Moses commanded, “Let no man leave of it till the morning.”

easy.question: What happened to the manna that was left until morning?
answers: It hardened
It bred worms and stank
It became sweeter
easy.explanation: The manna that was left bred worms and became foul.

easy.question: When did the Israelites gather the manna?
answers: At night
At noon
In the morning
easy.explanation: The verse says that they gathered it every morning.

medium.question: Why was Moses angry with the Israelites?
answers: They disobeyed him and left manna until morning
They gathered too little manna
They gathered the manna at noon
medium.explanation: Moses was angry because some people disobeyed and left manna until morning.

medium.question: In the phrase “it bred worms, and stank,” what does “stank” mean?
answers: It became hard
It developed a bad smell
It became white
medium.explanation: “Stank” means that it became foul-smelling, as the spoiled manna did.

medium.question: What does the connection between gathering manna and the heat of the sun show?
answers: Manna could be gathered only at night
Manna became tastier as the sun grew hot
The manna had to be gathered in the morning before it melted in the heat
medium.explanation: The Israelites gathered it in the morning; when the sun grew hot, it melted.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from the contrast between Moses’ command and the result of leaving manna?
answers: Manna was intended for daily gathering, not storage until the next day
Manna was intended only for leaders
Manna remained good for several days
challenge.explanation: The command and the spoilage show that manna was meant for daily use.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “every man according to his eating” mean?
answers: Everyone gathered exactly the same amount
Each person gathered according to the amount of food he needed
Only adults gathered manna
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that each person’s amount matched his food needs.

challenge.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: The manna melted, then they gathered it, and finally Moses commanded them
The people gathered at night, the manna spoiled, and then the sun came up
Moses commanded them not to leave any, some left it and it spoiled, and in the morning they gathered it before it melted
challenge.explanation: The sequence is Moses’ command, disobedience and spoilage, and morning gathering before the heat of the sun.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from the contrast between Moses’ command and the result of leaving manna?
answers: Manna was intended for daily gathering, not storage until the next day
Manna was intended only for leaders
Manna remained good for several days
questions.explanation: The command and the spoilage show that manna was meant for daily use.

questions.question: What does the phrase “every man according to his eating” mean?
answers: Everyone gathered exactly the same amount
Each person gathered according to the amount of food he needed
Only adults gathered manna
questions.explanation: The phrase means that each person’s amount matched his food needs.

questions.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: The manna melted, then they gathered it, and finally Moses commanded them
The people gathered at night, the manna spoiled, and then the sun came up
Moses commanded them not to leave any, some left it and it spoiled, and in the morning they gathered it before it melted
questions.explanation: The sequence is Moses’ command, disobedience and spoilage, and morning gathering before the heat of the sun.

paragraphs.title: The Double Portion and Preparation for the Sabbath

easy.question: On which day did the Israelites gather twice as much bread?
answers: The sixth day
The first day
The seventh day
easy.explanation: On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread.

easy.question: What was special about the seventh day?
answers: More bread fell
There was no bread in the field
Everyone gathered double bread
easy.explanation: Moses said that on the seventh day they would not find bread in the field.

easy.question: What happened to the bread that was left until morning?
answers: It disappeared
It spoiled
It did not stink and had no worms
easy.explanation: The bread was kept safely until morning without spoiling.

medium.question: Why did the Israelites gather twice as much bread on the sixth day?
answers: Because they could not gather on the seventh day
Because the sixth day was a special festival
Because bread was scarce all week
medium.explanation: The seventh day was the Sabbath, so there would be no bread in the field to gather.

medium.question: In the phrase “lay up for you to be kept,” what does “kept” mean?
answers: Thrown away
Saved or stored
Shared with others
medium.explanation: The context shows that the bread was to be saved until morning.

medium.question: What was the correct order of actions on the sixth day?
answers: They ate everything, then gathered, and finally cooked
They waited for the Sabbath and then went out to gather
They gathered twice as much, prepared the food, and stored the extra
medium.explanation: They gathered twice as much, baked and boiled it, and stored what remained until morning.

challenge.question: What does the fact that the bread kept until morning without stinking or developing worms show?
answers: The bread was specially preserved for the Sabbath
The bread was eaten immediately
The bread was made from a different material
challenge.explanation: Unlike manna left on an ordinary day, this portion was preserved for the Sabbath.

challenge.question: What change occurred in gathering bread between the six days and the seventh day?
answers: They did not gather during the six days
They gathered during the six days, but there was nothing to gather on the seventh
They gathered more on the seventh day than on any other
challenge.explanation: They gathered for six days, but there was no bread in the field on the seventh day.

challenge.question: Why did the rulers of the congregation tell Moses about what they had gathered on the sixth day?
answers: They wanted to leave the camp
They wanted to stop gathering bread
The double amount was unusual and needed an explanation
challenge.explanation: The unusually large amount gathered on the sixth day led them to report it to Moses.

questions.question: What does the fact that the bread kept until morning without stinking or developing worms show?
answers: The bread was specially preserved for the Sabbath
The bread was eaten immediately
The bread was made from a different material
questions.explanation: Unlike manna left on an ordinary day, this portion was preserved for the Sabbath.

questions.question: What change occurred in gathering bread between the six days and the seventh day?
answers: They did not gather during the six days
They gathered during the six days, but there was nothing to gather on the seventh
They gathered more on the seventh day than on any other
questions.explanation: They gathered for six days, but there was no bread in the field on the seventh day.

questions.question: Why did the rulers of the congregation tell Moses about what they had gathered on the sixth day?
answers: They wanted to leave the camp
They wanted to stop gathering bread
The double amount was unusual and needed an explanation
questions.explanation: The unusually large amount gathered on the sixth day led them to report it to Moses.

paragraphs.title: The Sabbath Test and the People’s Rest

easy.question: On which day did some people go out to gather and find nothing?
answers: The seventh day
The first day
The sixth day
easy.explanation: On the seventh day some people went out to gather, but found nothing.

easy.question: What did the Lord give the people on the sixth day?
answers: Bread for one day
Bread for two days
Bread for a week
easy.explanation: The Lord gave them twice as much bread on the sixth day so they would have enough for the Sabbath.

easy.question: What did the Israelites do on the seventh day?
answers: They went out to gather
They collected extra bread
They rested
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying that the people rested on the seventh day.

medium.question: Why did the Lord give bread for two days on the sixth day?
answers: Because the people would not go out to gather on the seventh day
Because there was a shortage of bread
Because the people were traveling elsewhere
medium.explanation: The extra bread allowed the people to rest on the seventh day instead of gathering.

medium.question: In the question “How long refuse ye to keep my commandments?”, what does “refuse” mean?
answers: Agreed
Declined or disobeyed
Rejoiced
medium.explanation: “Refuse” means to reject or decline; the Lord rebuked the people for not keeping His commandments.

medium.question: What was the purpose of the command “abide ye every man in his place”?
answers: To tell everyone to remain in his place on the Sabbath
To tell the people to search for food
To tell the people to move to a new camp
medium.explanation: The command told the people to stay where they were and not go out to gather on the seventh day.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the Lord giving “the bread of two days” on the sixth day?
answers: The Sabbath required preparation beforehand
The Sabbath lasted two days
The people received bread only on the Sabbath
challenge.explanation: The double portion allowed the people to prepare in advance and rest on the seventh day.

challenge.question: What does “How long” express in the Lord’s words to Moses?
answers: A promise of future help
Wonder and rebuke over continued disobedience
Joy that the commandments were being kept
challenge.explanation: The question asks how long the Israelites would continue refusing to keep the Lord’s commandments.

challenge.question: What distinguishes the sixth day from the seventh day in this chapter?
answers: No bread was given on the sixth day
Everyone went out to gather on the seventh day
Double bread was given on the sixth day, and the people rested on the seventh
challenge.explanation: The people gathered a two-day supply on the sixth day and rested instead of gathering on the seventh.

questions.question: What can we infer from the Lord giving “the bread of two days” on the sixth day?
answers: The Sabbath required preparation beforehand
The Sabbath lasted two days
The people received bread only on the Sabbath
questions.explanation: The double portion allowed the people to prepare in advance and rest on the seventh day.

questions.question: What does “How long” express in the Lord’s words to Moses?
answers: A promise of future help
Wonder and rebuke over continued disobedience
Joy that the commandments were being kept
questions.explanation: The question asks how long the Israelites would continue refusing to keep the Lord’s commandments.

questions.question: What distinguishes the sixth day from the seventh day in this chapter?
answers: No bread was given on the sixth day
Everyone went out to gather on the seventh day
Double bread was given on the sixth day, and the people rested on the seventh
questions.explanation: The people gathered a two-day supply on the sixth day and rested instead of gathering on the seventh.

paragraphs.title: The Name and Description of Manna

easy.question: What name did the Israelites give the food?
answers: Manna
Gad
Honey
easy.explanation: The Israelites called the food manna.

easy.question: What did manna look like?
answers: A wafer made with honey
White coriander seed
Bread
easy.explanation: The verse describes it as white coriander seed.

easy.question: What did manna taste like?
answers: Salt
Oil
Wafers made with honey
easy.explanation: The verse says that its taste was like wafers made with honey.

medium.question: Which description correctly gives both the appearance and taste of manna?
answers: It looked like white coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey
It looked like honey and tasted like coriander seed
It both looked and tasted like wafers
medium.explanation: The verse separately describes its appearance as white coriander seed and its taste as honey wafers.

medium.question: In the phrase “the taste of it was like wafers made with honey,” what are wafers?
answers: Small grains
Thin sweet cakes or crackers
White plants
medium.explanation: The context of honey and taste indicates a sweet cake or thin cracker.

medium.question: Which phrase describes manna’s appearance rather than its taste?
answers: Like wafers made with honey
The taste of it
Like white coriander seed
medium.explanation: “White coriander seed” describes its appearance, while honey wafers describe its taste.

challenge.question: Why does the verse use two different comparisons for manna?
answers: To describe its appearance and taste separately
To say that it had two names
To compare it with two colors
challenge.explanation: The comparison to coriander seed describes its appearance, and the comparison to honey wafers describes its taste.

challenge.question: What does “it” refer to in the description of manna?
answers: The house of Israel
Manna
Coriander seed
challenge.explanation: After manna is mentioned, “it” continues the description of that same food.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the order in which the verse describes manna?
answers: Its taste is described first and its name afterward
Its color is described first and then who ate it
Its name is given first, then its appearance, and finally its taste
challenge.explanation: The verse moves from the name manna, to its appearance, and finally to its taste.

questions.question: Why does the verse use two different comparisons for manna?
answers: To describe its appearance and taste separately
To say that it had two names
To compare it with two colors
questions.explanation: The comparison to coriander seed describes its appearance, and the comparison to honey wafers describes its taste.

questions.question: What does “it” refer to in the description of manna?
answers: The house of Israel
Manna
Coriander seed
